status: Complete higher-order template source/test review; conditional-adapter limitation identified for follow-up.
insights: Miller abstraction accepts function holes only on distinct locally bound variables. It remaps deBruijn indices under nested lambdas and rejects dependence on unabstracted locals; free captured values remain explicit.
Repeated hole bindings must be equal and parameter/concrete callback types unify. Structural discovery cannot assume arbitrary lambda equivalence.
Type instantiation and exact-source adapter construction are distinct phases. Adapters compose ordinary normalization with a Use proof of an instantiated base law, preserving database authority.

Generated law dependencies are authenticated through snapshot-owned objects, limited to4096templates,64dependencies/template,depth16and1024instantiated objects. Type cache keys include template identity and complete bindings; cached dependency height still participates in depth checks.
Adapter cache keys include base identity and exact target. Open local sites and conflicting free-variable sorts are rejected; nominal definitions are rebound to exact core/subject.

A current explicit limitation skips higher-order exact adapters when base conditions are nonempty. General conditional callback laws may need substituted adapter conditions and explicit premise replay, rather than dropping conditions or trusting a matched template. This needs an actual admitted conditional fixture before implementation.

Existing tests verify permutation/nesting/capture rejection, repeated-variable rejection, real endpoint adapter admission and rehashed false-adapter rejection. These checks do not cover conditional higher-order adapters.
next: Reproduce a useful conditional higher-order adapter case; investigate constructing substituted conditions with ordinary Hypothesis/Use proof composition. Preserve normal premise synthesis and exact source checks. No such extension is implemented or claimed yet.
